question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: A path is VALID when it is one or more NAMES joined by "/", it does not start with "/", it holds no backslash, and no NAME is empty, "." or "..". So "", "/abs", "a\b", "a//b", "./a", "a/.", "../x", "a/../b" and "a/" are INVALID; "...", ".hidden" and "a b" are ordinary NAMES.

If any path of files is INVALID -> throws. The message is the text "tree_sha: not a relative path " followed by the path as a JSON string literal (the message is informative, not graded). No hash is computed. CITED FIDELITY package — the seam refuses before it writes

Build output is excluded: a path with at least two NAMES whose FIRST NAME is exactly "target" contributes nothing (the crate-root target directory). Everything else is kept: a root FILE named "target", a "target" directory below the root ("src/target/x.rs"), a file "src/target", and any other spelling ("Target", "TARGET", "targets", "target.rs"). CITED FIDELITY package
Each kept path p yields one LINE: p exactly as given, then U+0000, then HEX(SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the file's text), then U+000A. An empty text hashes as the SHA-256 of zero bytes.

The LINES are sorted ascending by the whole line, comparing UTF-16 code units as unsigned integers (lexicographic, a proper prefix first). Because no path holds U+0000, this equals sorting the paths themselves by UTF-16 code units over the FULL path text — never NAME by NAME and never by UTF-8 bytes. So "a-b" < "a.b" < "a/b" (U+002D, U+002E, U+002F), and U+1F600 (units D83D DE00) sorts BEFORE U+E000 and U+FFFD, the reverse of their UTF-8 byte order. CITED FIDELITY package — the host's default string sort
The result is HEX(SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of T), T being the sorted LINES concatenated with no separator. With no kept path T is empty and the result is HEX of the SHA-256 of zero bytes.
SHA-256 is the FIPS 180-4 hash. HEX renders a 32-byte digest as 64 characters, two per byte, most significant nibble first, digits 0-9 and lowercase a-f.
